texts.passage: Notice from the school shop: This Friday, students may bring clean reusable bags to receive a small discount on stationery. The offer does not apply to textbooks or electronic devices. Please check the final price on the receipt before leaving the counter.
texts.statement: The school-shop discount includes electronic devices.

texts.passage: Dear Huda, I bought a camera bag yesterday, but the zip broke during the first use. I have kept my receipt and have not attempted to repair it. Could you accompany me to the shop after school so I can explain the problem?
texts.statement: The writer has already repaired the broken zip.

texts.passage: A local market has introduced clearly marked price labels for handmade baskets. Visitors may still ask questions about materials, but sellers agreed to show one final price per item. Organisers hope that transparent prices will help customers compare products more confidently.
texts.statement: Sellers at the market now display a final price for each basket.

texts.passage: Advertisement: Our recycled notebooks are made from carefully selected leftover paper. Each notebook contains eighty pages, and every cover has a different design. Customers can see sample books in the shop before ordering. Delivery charges are shown separately at checkout.

rdg2.title: Reading 2: Interactive emails
rdg2.passage:
Email 1 — From Amal to Green Market Online

Dear Customer Service Team,

Last Monday I ordered a study lamp from your website because the advertisement showed a significant discount. The description said the lamp could be charged by USB, and the photograph included a charging cable. My parcel arrived on Thursday, but the box contained no cable. The lamp itself seems undamaged. I checked the order confirmation, and I cannot find a sentence clearly explaining that the cable is sold separately.

I would like to know whether the missing cable can be supplied without an extra charge. If that is not possible, please explain the return procedure and whether I must pay delivery costs. I have kept the receipt, the packaging and a copy of the advertisement.

Kind regards,
Amal

Email 2 — From Customer Service to Amal

Dear Amal,

Thank you for explaining the problem clearly and sending the order number. We have reviewed your purchase. The USB cable is listed under optional accessories in the full product description, but we agree that our main photograph may have created a misleading impression. We will make the wording more obvious for future customers.

You may choose one of two options. We can send a compatible cable free of charge, or you may return the lamp within fourteen days of delivery. If you choose the return, we will provide a prepaid label and refund the original purchase price after the item has been checked. Please do not send the parcel before receiving the label.

Sincerely,
Green Market Online Support

Email 3 — From Amal to Customer Service

Dear Support Team,

Thank you for your prompt response. I appreciate your decision to improve the advertisement. I would prefer to receive the free cable because the lamp suits my desk and I do not want a working product to be wasted. Please confirm the delivery address already attached to my order and tell me when the cable is expected.

I will keep the original receipt and show your message to our school's consumer-awareness group. We are studying how clear descriptions and fair return policies can prevent misunderstandings. Your explanation will help us discuss both the customer's responsibilities and the seller's duties.

Best wishes,
Amal

rdg3.title: Reading 3: Consumer choices
rdg3.passage:
People often think that a low price automatically makes a purchase a good decision. In reality, responsible shopping involves several separate questions. A buyer should consider whether an item is needed, how long it may last, what the complete cost will be and what happens if the product develops a fault. These questions apply to traditional markets, shopping centres and online stores.

Advertisements can provide useful information, but their main purpose is often to persuade customers. A slogan might draw attention to a large discount without mentioning delivery fees or accessories that must be bought separately. Good shoppers therefore read the detailed description and compare similar products. They also recognise that an attractive photograph cannot demonstrate the quality of an item on its own.

A receipt is another important part of a purchase. It normally shows the date, amount paid and details of the product. Keeping a receipt helps a customer explain a problem accurately and may be necessary when asking for an exchange or refund. In an online transaction, the confirmation email can serve a similar purpose. Customers should save this information in a safe place rather than share private payment details publicly.

Consumers must also understand the difference between a warranty and a return policy. A warranty may explain what happens if a product stops working under certain conditions, while a return policy describes when the shop will accept an item back. The exact rules can differ, so assumptions based on another seller's policy may be unreliable. Asking a clear question before payment is usually easier than solving a misunderstanding afterwards.

Responsible shopping also has environmental and community benefits. Repairing an item, choosing durable materials or using a reusable bag can reduce unnecessary waste. Buying from a local seller may make it easier to inspect goods and ask about their origin, although local products are not automatically better in every situation. What matters is comparing evidence rather than relying on a single attractive claim.

Students can practise these skills by examining two advertisements for similar products. They can identify the essential features, calculate the total price and discuss which questions remain unanswered. Such exercises teach financial awareness and careful communication. The goal is not to avoid every purchase, but to make decisions that are informed, fair and suitable for a person's actual needs.

Every school can develop these habits through classroom discussions, consumer-awareness workshops and community projects that involve both families and students.
